title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Nauru: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Nauru: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Nauru: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Planning healthcare, employment, superannuation, civil identity, and estate matters in advance in Nauru ensures families have clear instructions and verified records ready under domestic statutes. Because Nauru's legislative archive (ronlaw.gov.nr) uses an interactive viewer and ministry websites mainly publish agency directories rather than step-by-step online guides, this checklist is built directly from primary Nauru laws, Government directories, Naoero Super publications, and accredited regional guidance [1][2][4][5][7].

steps.title: Healthcare coordination, local capacity limits, and statutory leave
steps.html:
• Coordinate clinical care, treatment planning, and any overseas medical referral approvals through the Republic of Nauru Hospital, noting local emergency telephone numbers (118 for medical ambulance; 117 for police and fire) [10][11]. Discuss realistic care options early with the treating physician, as regional consular guidance notes limited on-island hospital mortuary storage and absence of embalming or cremation infrastructure [10].
  • For Republic of Nauru public officers, check statutory leave entitlements under the Public Service Act 2016: employees receive 10 days of paid medical leave per year (non-cumulative, with a medical certificate required for absences exceeding 1 day under Sections 55 and 56), 3 days of paid special leave per year for sufficient cause (Section 71), 4 weeks of annual recreation leave (Section 49, up to 3 years' accrual), and up to 12 months of leave without pay (Section 77), alongside long service leave (12 weeks per 10 years of continuous service under Section 79) [5].
  • Check medical retirement provisions under Sections 86 to 88 and 101 to 103 of the Public Service Act 2016 (which provide 4 weeks' salary in lieu of notice plus accrued annual and long service leave), as well as the Chief Secretary's gratuity power under Section 103(3) added by the Public Service (Amendment) Act 2018 [5][6].

steps.title: Estate planning, Curator rules, and land-tenure clarity
steps.html:
• Prepare or review a valid written Will addressing personal assets, bank balances, and household property while capacity is clear [2]. Note that under the Succession, Probate and Administration Act 1976, if a person leaves no local executor or no probate application is lodged within 3 months, estate administration passes to Office of the Curator of Intestate Estates (justice.gov.nr), where Gazette publication and a 21-day waiting period apply before distribution [2].
  • Separate personal financial property from customary Nauruan land interests, which remain subject to the Nauru Lands Committee and local court jurisdiction rather than unilateral private transfer [2].
  • Because Nauru does not operate an automated online registry for enduring healthcare directives, state care wishes clearly with the attending physician and trusted family members while also organizing written financial authority if banking access is needed [2][10].

steps.title: Naoero Super (SuperLife) nominations and TPD withdrawal planning
steps.html:
• Verify active member details, employer contributions, and beneficiary records with Naoero Super (SuperLife), reviewing the Naoero Super at a Glance brochure and the Death and TPD Withdrawal Form [7][8][9].
  • If a member becomes totally and permanently unable to work due to illness or disability, check Total and Permanent Disablement (TPD) withdrawal documentation rules under Naoero Super early so required medical practitioner certifications are gathered accurately [7][8].
  • Store membership IDs and beneficiary relationship records alongside banking particulars (such as Bendigo Bank agency account details on Nauru) [2][7].

steps.title: Vital status alignment and Nauru Revenue Office compliance
steps.html:
• Verify spelling consistency across birth records, marriage records, passports, and employment files held through Department of Justice and Border Control (which houses the Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 2017) [1][3].
  • Check employment tax and business filing compliance with Nauru Revenue Office (First Floor, Civic Centre, Aiwo; +674 557 3238; cashier Monday to Thursday 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM, Friday 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM) [4]. Nauru does not impose a separate inheritance or estate tax [4].
  • Keep original identity papers, employment contracts, and account files together in one verified location [2][4][5].

steps.title: Cross-border legalisation readiness and family inventory
steps.html:
• If family members, superannuation funds, or overseas bank accounts sit outside Nauru, remember that Nauru is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [12]. Certified vital records and court documents for foreign institutions therefore require diplomatic or consular legalisation rather than an Apostille [12].
  • Prepare a concise household inventory covering Naoero Super numbers, public-service HR contacts, bank accounts, insurance policies, land committee references, and original document storage [2][4][7].
  • Verify notice and identity procedures directly with Nauru Media Corporation or utility providers where service accounts must later be updated [4][13].
